thesis.value: No wave in Texas: turnout is tracking the 2018 midterm, when Cruz won, at or slightly above its pace per registered voter, far above it only in raw ballots because registration grew. Democrats front-loaded: by primary history early voters went from D+6.8 after Monday to R+0.2 through Friday, and more reliable Republican than Democratic primary voters have yet to vote, the late-Republican pattern Big Data Poll’s respondents described (Democrats early, Republicans later); the three in ten early voters with no primary history decide how far it goes.
thesis.source: Intellz reading of the evidence [I]: method, grades and every source
thesis.note: Intellz reading of the evidence (25 Oct): turnout pace per registered voter is measured against the 2018 midterm; primary history describes who has voted; the stated strategy is sourced on the coverage page (Baris, 23 Oct).

claims.claim: Media coverage of a massive Democratic wave is overblown.
Four polling firms faked polls, and those polls pushed the averages toward Democrats.
Democrats front-load the first week of early voting.
Republicans show up late, as with Cruz and Beto in 2018.

value.part: The "massive Democratic wave" coverage is overblown
value.qualifier: Texas: largely yes; nationally: the Democratic environment is real. Intellz read: the surge headlines measure against 2024, Republicans’ best early-vote year. Against the midterms, Texas is on the 2018 pace per registered voter and the 22-state party mix is flat with 2022. In our backtest of past state races the final polls missed toward Democrats by about 2 points on average, and the party-registration lead the media cites missed the result by 16..

value.part: Democrats flooded week 1 to pull non-primary, non-midterm voters onto the bandwagon and depress Republicans
value.qualifier: The front-load is real and it is primary voters; the bandwagon and "depress" parts are not shown. The strategy is stated, not inferred: Rich Baris (Big Data Poll, on X, 23 Oct): "DEM IPEV wanted to vote ASAP, Republicans later" [V]. The data show the front-load: by primary history Monday’s voters leaned D+5.5, Friday’s R+3.0, and the total is now even, with the larger pool of reliable Republican primary voters still to vote (688K against 351K)..

2016.source: Intellz estimate [E]: the SOS 2016 15-county daily curve, scaled to the statewide early vote in the SOS 2016 race summary report (president) and the November 2016 registration
2016.note: ESTIMATED, not counted: the SOS 15-county 2016 daily curve as a share of its final, times the statewide early vote (6,564,197, president, SOS race summary), over the November 2016 registration (15,101,087). Back-test: run on 2020, 2022 and 2024, where the real statewide series exists, the same scaling missed it by at most 0.69 points of registration on any day (up to 5% of the count in the first days), and on day 5 it ran 0.40 to 0.55 points low in 2022 and 2024. So read a gap of less than about half a point between 2026 and a dashed line as no gap.

scenarios.source: Transparency USA / JPM Strategies Texas turnout tracker (primary-history pools)
scenarios.note: Scenario arithmetic, not a projection: IF primary-history voters vote their label and turnout lands at each scenario's level. Never backtested, and the party labels themselves misclassify a share of voters. Final turnout: A = the 2022 share of registered, B = VoteHub's implied total, C = 55.7% of registered; D and E test the theory. Breakeven = the margin (R minus D) no-primary voters must give for a tie under those assumptions: negative means they must break toward Talarico, positive toward Paxton.

need.source: Transparency USA / JPM Strategies Texas turnout tracker (primary-history pools)
need.note: Scenario arithmetic, not a projection (never backtested): IF primary-history voters vote their label, then for Talarico to win by 1.9 (VoteHub's forecast) no-primary voters would have to break D+6.5 (scenario B), D+8.2 (C) or D+8.7 (A), 8.7 to 10.9 points more Democratic than their model-implied R+2.2 for Cruz-Allred in 2024. A primary label is a proxy for party that misclassifies some voters, and its error is not measured here.

pool.rt_caveat: Read these as a reservoir that can show up, not as votes. The unvoted Republican-primary pool includes March primary voters who backed Cornyn against Paxton, and the larger Republican primary inflates the Republican stock; both parties' March early voters have turned out at about the same rate so far (Republicans 56.6%, Democrats 57.3%); the tracker covers 243 of 254 counties.

edday.note: Early = early in person plus mail ballots, as Texas reports them. ED minus early above zero means Election Day was more Republican than the early vote.
edday.rt_note: Election Day ran redder than the early vote in 7 of 10 top statewide races since 2014, by 2.1 to 17.1 points. The exceptions: 2016 President (2.1 points more Democratic on Election Day), 2018 Senate (0.3 points more Democratic on Election Day), 2024 Senate (4.1 points more Democratic on Election Day). Both Cruz Senate races are among them, so Election Day is no rescue by habit; it turns on who has not voted yet and how they break.
